text.p: Meatpacking giant IBP Corp. Monday reported lower profits for the fourth quarter and cited an unexpected decline in exports and plant start-up costs.

IBP, the world's largest producer of fresh beef and pork products, said its profits fell to $18 million, or 19 cents per share, in the fourth quarter from $35 million, or 36 cents per share, a year earlier.
Revenues fell to $3.02 billion from $3.16 billion.

"Changing livestock supplies, an unexpected decline in exports and plant start up expenses contributed to tough comparisons in the second half of the year," IBP Chairman Robert Peterson said in a statement.
IBP said tight hog supplies, coupled with a substantial expansion of the nation's pork processing capacity, continued to hurt its pork operations.
For all of 1996 net earnings totalled $199 million compared to $258 million in 1995 on revenues of $12.5 billion vs. $12.7 billion the previous year.
The Dakota City, Neb.-based company said its international sales declined for the first time in more than a decade, with 1996 net export sales down 8 percent from 1995 at $1.7 billion.
The company cited concerns about "mad cow " disease and an e. coli outbreak in Japan for the drop in exports. It said shipment to Japan had begun to return to more normal levels.
